name: Texas US Senate Republican Primary Runoff

priorComponents.description: All inputs to the pre-count expected shift, with citations. The shift is added to the no-swing R1 head-to-head baseline.

polls.note: First post-endorsement poll. Single-pollster, possibly R-house effect — downweighted in blend.

endorsement.note: Trump endorsement of MAGA-aligned challenger in GOP runoff. Hopkins/Lelkes 2024 and FiveThirtyEight historical tracking put GOP-primary Trump-endorsement effects in the +3 to +10pp range.

huntRedistribution.note: Hunt was the R1 #3 candidate (MAGA-aligned). Pre-endorsement polls (UH) already had respondents redistributing Hunt voters in their stated preferences, so this is ENCODED IN POLLS, not added separately.

derivation.method: Inverse-variance weighted polling average, with pre-endorsement polls adjusted by literature-midpoint endorsement effect, plus between-poll heterogeneity τ and polls-to-actual error.
derivation.note: expectedShiftFinal rounded slightly conservative vs. raw weighted mean to give appropriate weight to the larger-sample UH poll's adjusted estimate; SD rounded up to 8 to allow for the wider tail.

turnoutModel.description: Turnout weight per county = α × (EV share) + (1-α) × (R1 share). EV through close of early voting 5/22/2026; α = 0.55 reflects historical TX primary-runoff EV-as-share-of-total turnout (50–65% range).

source.name: Texas Secretary of State — Early Voting Turnout Portal

turnoutModel.alphaJustification: TX primary-runoff EV typically 50–65% of total turnout (2018, 2020, 2022, 2024 runoffs). 0.55 is the midpoint estimate; the prior's σ=8pp absorbs alpha uncertainty.
